deals.foreign_party: Aiolos Bio (later acquired by GSK for $1.4B)
deals.equity_component: Hengrui received no equity in Aiolos — key lesson that led to equity retention in all subsequent NewCo deals
deals.highlights: The original China NewCo deal — Hengrui licensed its TSLP antibody to newly formed Aiolos Bio for just $25M upfront, which raised $245M from VCs. Only three months later GSK acquired Aiolos for $1B+$400M earn-out, with all windfall going to VCs. Hengrui received nothing from the sale. This deal defined the NewCo model and taught Chinese companies to always retain equity.

The largest upfront payment for a China-originating out-licensing deal in 2023 at $800M. BMS secured ex-China rights to this EGFRxHER3 bispecific ADC, which subsequently posted positive Phase 3 results in China and encouraging early global trial data (55% ORR). The deal cemented China's position as a leading source of ADC innovation for global pharma.

Roche's return to ADCs after years of publicly expressing limited interest, kickstarted by licensing MediLink's c-MET-targeting ADC YL211. The deal marked a shift in Roche's strategy after Enhertu trounced Kadcyla in head-to-head trials, and signaled China as a critical ADC innovation hub for the Swiss pharma giant.

BioNTech expanded its existing MediLink collaboration (first deal in Oct 2023 for HER3 ADC at $70M upfront), paying $25M upfront to access MediLink's TMALIN platform for several BioNTech-selected targets. The deal has up to $1.8B in milestones and reflects BioNTech's strategy to build a broad ADC pipeline partially sourced from China.

deals.foreign_party: Kailera Therapeutics (formerly Hercules CM NewCo; backed by Bain Capital, RTW, Atlas Venture, Lyra Capital)
deals.asset: HRS-7535 (oral GLP-1, Phase 2), HRS-9531 (GLP-1/GIP dual agonist, Phase 2), HRS-4729 (preclinical) — obesity/diabetes portfolio
deals.highlights: Hengrui's second NewCo and the most prominent China spinout to date. After losing all upside from the Aiolos/GSK deal, Hengrui retained a 19.9% equity stake this time. The $400M VC round (Bain $225M, RTW $110M, Atlas $50M, Lyra $15M) was one of the largest NewCo launches ever. Renamed Kailera Therapeutics in October 2024 with veteran CEO Ron Renaud and Gilead's former CEO John Milligan as board chair.

BioNTech licensed ex-China rights to Biotheus's PM8002, a PD-L1/VEGF bispecific antibody in Phase 2 for solid tumors, for $55M upfront and over $1B in milestones. The bispecific aims to combine immune checkpoint inhibition with anti-angiogenesis in a single molecule, potentially offering differentiated efficacy with reduced toxicity. BioNTech continues building its oncology pipeline from Chinese innovators.

AstraZeneca licensed LaNova's GPRC5D-targeting ADC for multiple myeloma for $55M upfront. GPRC5D is an emerging target in hematologic malignancies, and this early deal predated LaNova's larger deals with Merck. This was one of LaNova's first major licensing agreements, validating its innovative ADC platform capabilities.

GSK paid $500M upfront to enter a wide-ranging alliance with Hengrui spanning COPD, immunology and cancer drugs, with total deal value up to $12.5B. One of the largest China biotech licensing deals ever, it reflects GSK's strategic bet on validated Chinese targets to rebuild its pipeline. Hengrui continues to establish itself as one of China's most prolific out-licensing partners.

deals.asset: CM512 and CM536 (two bispecific antibody candidates for autoimmune diseases)
deals.highlights: Keymed Biosciences' first NewCo deal, following Hengrui's playbook but with stronger equity terms — a 30% stake vs Hengrui's 19.9% in Kailera. OrbiMed created Belenos as a Delaware-incorporated autoimmunity-focused NewCo. Two bispecific antibody candidates with undisclosed targets licensed for $15M upfront and up to $170M in milestones.

Instil Bio licensed ex-China rights to ImmuneOnco Biopharma's IMM2510, a PD-L1/VEGF bispecific antibody, in August 2024. The drug has shown promising early data in China in lung cancer, and the FDA approved a Phase 1b/2 trial in the US. This was an early entry in the PD-1/VEGF bispecific wave that later attracted Pfizer/3SBio and BMS/BioNTech mega-deals, validating China as the originator of this mechanism.

deals.asset: CDK inhibitor portfolio (RGT-419B and preclinical candidate)
deals.highlights: Roche/Genentech paid $850M upfront to acquire Regor's next-generation CDK inhibitor portfolio, aimed at overcoming resistance to existing CDK4/6 inhibitors like Ibrance and Verzenio. RGT-419B showed durable single-agent activity in CDK-resistant patients. This was one of the largest China-origin asset acquisitions of 2024 and signals Roche's commitment to sourcing innovation from China.

Novartis' initial licensing agreements with Chinese RNAi specialist Argo Biopharma included $185M in upfront payments across two deals, establishing the collaboration that would later expand to $5.2B in 2025. This early bet on Argo highlights Novartis' strategy to build cardiovascular RNAi pipeline from Chinese innovation.

GSK signed its first Hansoh ADC deal at ESMO 2024 for a B7-H4-targeted ADC in solid tumors/gynecological cancer, paying $85M upfront plus up to $1.4B in milestones. GSK has since lined up five Phase 3 studies for this asset (GSK'584) to launch in H1 2026, demonstrating rapid clinical progression of China-originated ADCs by Big Pharma partners.

deals.asset: Preclinical cardiovascular disease drug (lipid-lowering oral therapy)
deals.highlights: AstraZeneca licensed an oral lipid-lowering therapy from CSPC Pharmaceutical for $100M upfront and up to $1.92B total, marking their first licensing collaboration. This deal helped deepen the AstraZeneca-CSPC relationship that expanded into AI-enabled drug discovery in 2025 and eventually the blockbuster $18.5B obesity deal.

Merck paid a massive $588M upfront for LaNova's PD-1xVEGF bispecific LM-299 as a direct hedge against ivonescimab's threat to Keytruda. The $588M upfront for a Phase 1 asset is extraordinary, reflecting the strategic imperative for Merck to secure a Keytruda successor. This deal kicked off a PD-1xVEGF licensing wave that later saw Pfizer/3SBio and BMS/BioNTech follow suit.

Merck paid a massive $588M upfront to Shanghai-based LaNova Medicines for worldwide rights to an early-stage PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody. The deal valued at up to $3.3B was a direct response to ivonescimab's stunning Phase 3 victory over Keytruda in NSCLC. This deal is defensively strategic for Merck as it seeks to protect its $29.5B Keytruda franchise by pivoting to the next-gen PD-1/VEGF bispecific mechanism pioneered in China.

deals.therapeutic_area: Oncology – Lung Cancer, Sarcoma, Solid Tumors
deals.highlights: GSK's second Hansoh ADC deal (weeks after the B7-H4 pact) involved HS-20093, a B7-H3-targeting ADC with a topoisomerase inhibitor payload. Phase 1 data showed responses in SCLC, NSCLC, and sarcoma across heavily pretreated patients. The $185M upfront was among the largest ADC upfronts of 2024, and GSK has since progressed this asset (GSK'227) to Phase 3 in SCLC.

deals.asset: PM8002/BNT327 (PD-L1/VEGF bispecific antibody) + full Biotheus pipeline
deals.highlights: BioNTech acquired Chinese biotech Biotheus for $800M to gain full global control of PM8002/BNT327, a PD-L1/VEGF bispecific antibody. This followed an initial $55M licensing deal in 2023. The acquisition was triggered by ivonescimab's landmark victory over Keytruda, validating the PD-L1/VEGF mechanism. BioNTech later attracted BMS as a co-development partner in a $11.1B deal in June 2025, exponentially multiplying the value of the original Chinese asset.

BeiGene licensed in a CDK2 inhibitor from Ensem Therapeutics to complement its internally discovered Phase 1 CDK4 inhibitor, building a comprehensive cell cycle inhibitor portfolio for breast cancer. The deal highlights BeiGene's evolution from Chinese biotech to global pharma, actively licensing in Western-developed assets.

Merck entered the oral GLP-1 race by licensing Hansoh's preclinical HS-10535 for up to $2B with $112M upfront. Despite the asset being at preclinical stage, the substantial upfront reflects the intense demand for oral obesity drugs. This positions Merck alongside AstraZeneca (Eccogene) and Pfizer in sourcing oral weight-loss candidates from China.

Roche licensed Hansoh's CDH17-targeted ADC HS-20110 for up to $1.53B with $80M upfront. CDH17 is a novel target in colorectal cancer where Roche has deep experience (Avastin franchise). The deal highlights Roche's continued appetite for China-originated ADCs and validates the CDH17 target in GI oncology.

GSK secured an option on a preclinical DualityBio ADC candidate for GI tumors, paying $30M upfront/pre-option with up to $975M in milestones if exercised. This is GSK's second trip to China for ADCs, following its $270M upfront Hansoh deal for B7-H3/B7-H4 ADCs. DualityBio's ADC platform has attracted deals totaling over $4B from BioNTech, BeiGene, and others.

Ideaya paid $75M upfront for ex-Greater China rights to Hengrui's DLL3-directed ADC SHR-4849, establishing Ideaya in the competitive small cell lung cancer ADC space. The deal reflects Hengrui's prolific ADC pipeline and willingness to partner assets at early clinical stages. Ideaya planned to file a US IND in H1 2025.

Merck inked an immunology licensing pact with China's Curon Pharmaceutical, part of Merck's spree of China deals in late 2024 alongside Hansoh (obesity) and LaNova (oncology). This underscores Merck's broader strategy of leveraging Chinese biotech innovation across multiple therapeutic areas beyond oncology.

GSK returned to Chinese ADC developer DualityBio, paying $30M for an option on a preclinical ADC targeting gastrointestinal tumors. DualityBio has struck ADC deals worth over $4B with companies including BioNTech, BeiGene, and Adcendo. GSK also paid Hansoh $270M upfront in a separate ADC deal, illustrating the continued Western pharma appetite for Chinese ADC technology.

Eisai licensed Henlius's approved lung cancer PD-1 antibody Hansizhuang (serplulimab) for $75M upfront and up to $313M in milestones. This deal extends Japan-China pharma collaboration and gives Eisai a competitive checkpoint inhibitor. Henlius, a Fosun Pharma subsidiary, continues to monetize its biosimilar and innovative antibody portfolio internationally.

Roche returned to Innovent Biologics at the start of 2025 to license IBI3009, a DLL3-targeted ADC for solid tumors that had just entered Phase 1 dosing. This deal continues Roche's aggressive ADC acquisition strategy and underscores Innovent's growing position as a serial out-licensor to major pharma partners including Roche, Takeda, and Lilly.

Ouro Medicines licensed bispecific TCE OM336 from Chinese biotech Keymed Biosciences alongside its $120M Series A. The deal targets B cell-mediated immune diseases using T cell engager technology, extending the TCE modality beyond oncology into autoimmune. Ouro plans to enter the clinic in 2025.

Roche returned to MediLink just one year after their first deal, this time for a B7-H3-targeting ADC with $570M in near-term payments. YL201 showed promising ORR and survival benefits in second-line SCLC Phase 2 data. The deal deepens Roche's commitment to MediLink's TMALIN ADC platform and its China sourcing strategy.

deals.asset: SYH2082 and portfolio of up to 8 obesity programs (GLP1R/GIPR agonists)
deals.highlights: AstraZeneca struck one of the largest China-originated licensing deals ever, paying $1.2B upfront for CSPC's portfolio of up to 8 next-generation weight management programs led by SYH2082, a long-acting GLP1R/GIPR agonist. The $18.5B total potential value is the largest China out-licensing deal scope since 2025, reflecting AZ's aggressive obesity strategy.

AbbVie struck a massive up to $5.6B licensing deal with Chinese ADC specialist RemeGen for an experimental tumor treatment. RemeGen is known for its ADC platform (including disitamab vedotin/Aidixi). This deal signals AbbVie's commitment to building an oncology pipeline via Chinese biotech partnerships and is one of the largest China out-licensing deals by total value.

AstraZeneca licensed an oral weight-loss pill from China's Eccogene as part of its broader obesity pipeline strategy, complementing its CSPC portfolio deal. Early clinical data showed the Eccogene pill may cause less muscle wastage than current GLP-1 treatments, a significant differentiator. The collaboration is part of AZ's multi-pronged China investment strategy targeting 20 new medicines by 2030.

deals.asset: Ivonescimab (PD-1xVEGF bispecific antibody) combination studies with Pfizer ADCs
deals.highlights: Summit and Pfizer partnered to test Akeso-originated ivonescimab alongside Pfizer's ADCs in combination studies seeking 'potentially landscape-changing combinations.' This partnership underscores ivonescimab's position as the frontrunner PD-1xVEGF bispecific and Big Pharma interest in pairing it with complementary modalities.

Pfizer partnered with Akeso and Summit Therapeutics to study ivonescimab alongside Pfizer's cancer pipeline medicines. This is a strategic combination trial arrangement rather than a full license, but notably it shows Pfizer hedging bets on PD-1xVEGF bispecifics by both partnering with the class leader (ivonescimab) and independently licensing a competitor from 3SBio.

deals.asset: HRS-5346 (oral heart disease drug / PCSK9 inhibitor)
deals.highlights: Merck paid $200M upfront for Hengrui's oral heart disease drug HRS-5346, an oral small molecule in mid-stage trials in China targeting cholesterol/lipid formation. This is Merck's third major China licensing deal in quick succession (after Hansoh obesity and LaNova oncology), signaling a systematic China sourcing strategy across therapeutic areas.

deals.asset: HRS-5346 (oral Lp(a) inhibitor for cardiovascular disease)
deals.highlights: Merck paid $200M upfront for rights outside Greater China to Hengrui's oral Lp(a) inhibitor HRS-5346, currently in Phase 2 testing. Hengrui is eligible for $1.77B in additional milestones plus royalties. The deal puts Merck in a competitive race against Novartis (RNA-based, Phase 3), Eli Lilly, and Amgen for this emerging cardiovascular drug class targeting a genetic risk factor believed to contribute to blood vessel blockages.

Novo Nordisk paid $200M upfront to China's United Laboratories for global ex-Greater China rights to UBT251, a GLP-1/GIP/glucagon triple agonist for obesity. Early Phase 2 data from China showed 19.7% weight loss, positioning UBT251 as a potential successor to Wegovy and rival to Lilly's retatrutide. The deal gives Novo critical 'triple G' optionality after CagriSema's underwhelming results, and reflects China's rapid emergence as a supplier of next-gen obesity drugs.

Sanofi licensed immune disease drugs from Chinese startup Earendil, expanding its autoimmune/immunology pipeline via China out-licensing. This deal reflects Sanofi's broader strategy to build a next-generation immunology portfolio, adding to the diversification of China deals beyond oncology into autoimmune indications.

Sanofi paid $125M upfront plus a $50M near-term payment for two autoimmune bispecific antibodies from Earendil Labs, a US-based AI biotech affiliated with China's Helixon Therapeutics. HXN-1002 targets α4β7/TL1A for IBD while HXN-1003 targets TL1A/IL23 for colitis and skin inflammation. The deal reflects Sanofi's ambition to become an 'immunoscience powerhouse' and the growing role of China-linked AI drug discovery platforms.

Sanofi licensed two bispecific antibodies from Earendil Labs, an affiliate of China-based AI antibody designer Helixon Therapeutics. HXN-1002 targets α4β7/TL1A for ulcerative colitis and Crohn's, while HXN-1003 targets TL1A/IL23 for colitis and skin inflammation. The deal is part of Sanofi's strategy to become an 'immunoscience powerhouse' and follows a broader trend of pharma companies accessing China's AI-driven drug discovery platforms. Sanofi later returned for a second deal with Earendil worth up to $2.56B.

deals.chinese_party: Earendil Labs (affiliate of Helixon Therapeutics, China)
deals.asset: Two bispecific drugs targeting TL1A/IL23 for autoimmune/IBD
deals.highlights: Sanofi paid $125M upfront plus $50M in near-term payments to Earendil Labs, an affiliate of China's Helixon Therapeutics, for two bispecific antibody candidates targeting popular immune disease targets TL1A and IL23. The deal could be worth up to $1.72B in additional milestones plus royalties. This signals Sanofi's interest in next-gen multi-targeting approaches for IBD/autoimmune, leveraging China's bispecific antibody design expertise.

Astellas doubled down on Claudin 18.2 less than a year after gaining the first anti-CLDN18.2 FDA approval (Vyloy). The $130M upfront with $70M in near-term milestones from Chinese biotech Evopoint positions Astellas to defend its lead in the competitive CLDN18.2 space with a next-gen ADC approach.

Pfizer paid a massive $1.25B upfront to 3SBio for ex-China rights to SSGJ-70, a PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody that competes with Akeso/Summit's ivonescimab and Merck's Keytruda. The deal also includes up to $4.8B in milestones plus a $100M equity investment and double-digit royalties. This is one of the largest China biotech out-licensing deals ever by upfront value, validating the PD-1/VEGF class.

Pfizer licensed a PD-1/VEGF cancer drug from Shenyang-based 3SBio, considered critical to Pfizer's future oncology plans. The deal was part of a broader wave in H1 2025 where one-third of all licensing deal spend involved China-originated medicines, up from 21% in 2023-2024. Pfizer's move into the PD-1/VEGF bispecific space puts it in competition with Akeso's ivonescimab and Biotheus' PM8002.

Pfizer paid $1.25B upfront plus $100M equity for ex-China rights to 3SBio's SSGJ-707, a PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody with up to $4.8B in milestones plus double-digit royalties. This slots Pfizer into the red-hot PD-1/VEGF bispecific race behind Summit/Akeso's ivonescimab and BioNTech's BNT327. SSGJ-707 is in four Phase 2 trials and set to enter Phase 3 in first-line PD-L1+ NSCLC in China.

Pfizer paid a massive $1.25B upfront for ex-China rights to 3SBio's PD-1xVEGF bispecific antibody, positioning it as a potential Keytruda challenger. This deal is part of the bispecific antibody wave in oncology, following the success of Akeso's ivonescimab. One of the largest upfront payments for a China-origin asset in 2025.

Regeneron entered the obesity race with a potential $2B deal for Hansoh Pharma's GLP-1/GIP agonist, aiming to challenge Eli Lilly's Zepbound. This deal signifies China's emergence as a source of next-gen metabolic therapies, not just oncology assets. Reflects the massive commercial opportunity in the obesity drug market.

Vor Bio pivoted from cell therapy to license RemeGen's telitacicept, a first-in-class BAFF/APRIL fusion protein already approved in China for autoimmune diseases. Despite $4B total value, the heavily back-loaded deal structure with only $45M upfront for an approved drug drew investor criticism, echoing the Hengrui-Aiolos dynamic where small upfronts undervalue Chinese assets.

NextCure licensed a Phase 1 ADC from Simcere as part of its strategic pivot toward ADCs, following its decision to abandon existing clinical candidates. This is Simcere's second major out-licensing deal after AbbVie's $1B trispecific antibody pact earlier in 2025, demonstrating Simcere's emergence as a multi-asset China out-licensing platform.

AbbVie struck a $1B biobucks deal with Simcere for a Phase 1 trispecific antibody, marking an early-stage but high-value bet on a novel multispecific format from China. Combined with the NextCure ADC deal, Simcere has now out-licensed two oncology assets in 2025 worth a combined $1.75B, establishing it as a prolific China licensing partner.

deals.asset: AI-driven oral drug discovery platform (immunological diseases and chronic conditions)
deals.highlights: AstraZeneca deepened its CSPC partnership with a $5.3B AI-led research collaboration to discover oral drugs for immunological and chronic diseases. CSPC will conduct AI-driven research in Shijiazhuang. This is AstraZeneca's third major CSPC deal after October 2024 cardiovascular and 2025 obesity deals, reflecting AZ's heavy commitment to Chinese biotech innovation and AI-enabled drug discovery.

deals.asset: AI-driven oral drug discovery platform for chronic diseases
deals.highlights: AstraZeneca returned to CSPC with $110M upfront to leverage CSPC's AI-driven dual-engine drug discovery platform to find oral drugs for chronic diseases. With up to $1.62B in development milestones and $3.6B in sales milestones, the deal deepens AZ's China-based R&D presence. CSPC's AI platform analyzes binding patterns of target proteins with existing compound molecules to identify those with highest clinical trial success probability.

Regeneron paid $80M upfront to Hansoh Pharma for ex-China rights to HS-20094, a Phase 3-stage GLP-1/GIP dual agonist with a 'potentially similar profile' to Eli Lilly's Zepbound. With up to $1.93B in milestones, the deal gives Regeneron a late-stage obesity asset to study in combination with its proprietary anti-activin antibody garetosmab. The deal tested in 1,000+ patients reflects China's rapid emergence in the GLP-1 obesity space.

deals.asset: HRS-9821 (dual PDE3/PDE4 inhibitor for COPD) plus options on 11 additional programs
deals.highlights: GSK paid a massive $500M upfront for Hengrui's inhaled PDE3/PDE4 inhibitor HRS-9821 for COPD, with options on 11 more programs across respiratory, oncology and immunology worth up to $12B total. This is one of the largest single-upfront China licensing deals ever, signaling that Hengrui has become a platform-level partner for Big Pharma. Jefferies noted one-third of industry licensing spending in H1 2025 involved China-originated drugs.

deals.asset: HRS-9821 (inhaled PDE3/PDE4 inhibitor for COPD) + options on up to 11 additional drugs
deals.highlights: GSK paid $500M upfront for Hengrui's COPD candidate HRS-9821 plus options on 11 additional therapies across respiratory, immunology and oncology. Total deal value could reach $12B if all options are exercised and milestones met. This is the largest and broadest platform deal from Hengrui, making it China's most prolific out-licensor. The deal underscores GSK's confidence in Hengrui's diverse pipeline and reflects the trend where 1/3 of pharma licensing spend in H1 2025 involved China-originated drugs.

Sino Biopharm acquired the ~95% of LaNova it didn't already own for up to $951M, marking a rare Chinese pharma acquiring an innovative domestic biotech. LaNova's pipeline includes eight clinical-stage compounds, with assets already out-licensed to Merck and AstraZeneca. This signals maturation of China's pharma M&A market.

deals.asset: Oncology portfolio (2 ADCs + 1 bispecific antibody including IBI3001)
deals.highlights: Takeda staked more than $11B in potential deal value on Innovent's cancer drugs, including ADCs and a bispecific targeting EGFR and B7H3 (IBI3001). This is a transformative deal for Takeda, which is rebuilding its oncology portfolio after losing exclusivity on top products like Vyvanse. The deal underscores China's emergence as a major source of innovative oncology assets for global pharma.

Sino Biopharm acquired LaNova Medicines, the Shanghai-based biotech founded less than 6 years ago that built a pipeline of 8 clinical-stage compounds including assets licensed to AstraZeneca and Merck. The acquisition demonstrates how rapidly Chinese biotechs can generate value – LaNova's assets include a GPRC5D ADC (licensed to AZ) and a PD-1/VEGF bispecific (licensed to Merck for $588M upfront).

deals.asset: LaNova Medicines (PD-1/VEGF bispecifics and cancer pipeline)
deals.highlights: Sino Biopharmaceutical acquired the remaining ~95% of LaNova Medicines it didn't own for up to $951M, gaining control of the company that had previously licensed PD-1/VEGF drugs to both Merck and AstraZeneca. LaNova's pipeline includes LM-299 (licensed to Merck), anti-SIRPa antibody, and multiple bispecifics. The deal represents intra-China consolidation at a time when Western pharma is paying billions for Chinese PD-1/VEGF assets.

deals.asset: Preclinical GLP-1 receptor agonist (for MASH combination)
deals.highlights: Madrigal paid CSPC $120M for a preclinical GLP-1 receptor agonist intended to be paired with its Rezdiffra MASH therapy. This was Madrigal's first China deal, preceding its February 2026 Ribo siRNA deal, as part of a broader strategy to build combination regimens around Rezdiffra. The deal highlights CSPC's expanding metabolic pipeline beyond its core obesity focus.

deals.asset: XH-S004 / EXPD-101 (DPP-1 inhibitor for COPD and bronchiectasis)
deals.territory: Global ex-mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau
deals.highlights: Expedition Therapeutics, a secretive US startup founded to in-license China assets, paid Fosun's S-Infinity subsidiary $17M upfront for ex-China rights to oral DPP-1 inhibitor XH-S004 with up to $645M total. The drug is in Phase 2 for bronchiectasis and Phase 1b for COPD in China, targeting the same mechanism as Insmed's newly approved Brinsupri (brensocatib). This was Expedition's debut deal, backed by Venrock, BVF and Lake Bleu Capital, and followed by a $165M Series A.

Boston-based Radiance Biopharma licensed rights to what Novatim claims is the first bispecific nano ADC (KY-0301). The technology promises better tumor tissue penetration and improved safety vs traditional bispecific ADCs. Reflects the continued ADC innovation wave coming out of China's biotech ecosystem.

Novartis signed a blockbuster $5.2B deal with China's Argo Biopharmaceutical for experimental cardiovascular genetic medicines targeting high blood fat levels and cholesterol. The deal includes a mid-stage genetic medicine plus options on two additional cholesterol candidates. Represents Novartis's aggressive move into cardiometabolic genetic therapies from Chinese innovation.

deals.asset: RNA cardiovascular portfolio (including BW-00112 RNAi drug)
deals.highlights: Novartis expanded its collaboration with Argo Biopharma, paying $160M upfront for a portfolio of RNAi cardiovascular drugs including options on discovery-stage molecules and right of first negotiation for BW-00112 (Phase 2). This builds on prior $185M deals from 2024, bringing total Novartis-Argo commitments to potentially billions. Signals growing non-oncology China out-licensing in cardiology via RNAi.

deals.asset: ADC for colorectal cancer and solid tumors
deals.highlights: Roche licensed a Hansoh ADC candidate targeting colorectal cancer and solid tumors for $80M upfront and up to $1.45B in milestones and royalties. This adds to Hansoh's growing deal portfolio, which includes the Merck GLP-1 deal and GSK ADC partnerships. Roche's CRC expertise (Avastin) makes this a strategic pipeline extension.

deals.territory: Global ex-China, US, Europe and select markets
deals.highlights: Hengrui licensed its China-approved HER2-directed ADC trastuzumab rezetecan to Glenmark Specialty for emerging markets excluding China, US, Europe and a few other regions. While the $18M upfront is modest, milestones of up to $1.09B reflect commercial potential. The ADC was approved in China in May 2025 for advanced NSCLC, demonstrating Hengrui's strategy of tiered regional licensing.

Boston-based Radiance Biopharma offered a Chinese firm over $1B for rights to a next-generation ADC, underscoring the premium that even emerging US biotechs are now willing to pay for Chinese-developed ADC technology. This deal reflects the continued boom in Chinese ADC out-licensing.

Novartis licensed RNA drugs from China-based Argo Biotherapeutics in a deal worth potentially over $5 billion, continuing its strategy of tapping Chinese biotech innovation. The deal targets ANGPTL3, a validated cardiovascular/metabolic target, and represents one of several deals Novartis has struck with China-based companies in recent years. The sizable deal value underscores growing confidence in Chinese RNA therapeutic platforms.

deals.asset: HRS-1893 / BHB-1893 (selective myosin inhibitor for HCM)
deals.highlights: Hengrui licensed its selective myosin inhibitor HRS-1893 to stealth startup Braveheart Bio, which later raised $185M Series A from Andreessen Horowitz, Forbion, OrbiMed, and others. The drug is positioned as a potential best-in-class challenger to Bristol Myers' Camzyos and Cytokinetics' aficamten. The deal is one of at least 20 between Chinese biotechs and privately held US/EU companies in 2025, reflecting a new model of startups being built entirely around China-licensed assets.

deals.asset: RNA drugs targeting ANGPTL3 and other targets
deals.highlights: Novartis struck a potentially $5B+ alliance with China-based Argo Biopharmaceutical for RNA drugs including ANGPTL3-targeting assets. This is one of several deals Novartis has made with Chinese biotechs in recent years, reflecting the Swiss pharma giant's willingness to tap China's RNA therapeutics innovation. The alliance significantly expands Novartis's RNA platform beyond its existing siRNA capabilities.

deals.equity_component: Equity stake in Kalexo Bio (amount undisclosed)
deals.highlights: Aditum Bio's incubator model created Kalexo Bio to advance Mabwell's dual-target siRNA candidate targeting lipid management. 2MW7141 demonstrated potent suppression of target genes in preclinical studies. Mabwell retains equity in Kalexo alongside up to $1B in milestones and royalties — following the equity-retention model pioneered after the Aiolos/GSK lesson.

deals.asset: IBI363 (PD-1/IL-2 bispecific) and IBI343 (Claudin 18.2 ADC), plus option on IBI3001 (EGFR/B7H3 ADC)
deals.highlights: One of the largest China biotech out-licensing deals ever, with $1.2B upfront and $100M equity investment from Takeda. The deal includes two late-stage cancer assets (IBI363 and IBI343) plus an option on early-stage IBI3001. Takeda views this as transformative for its post-Entyvio oncology growth strategy, with 60/40 cost and profit sharing in the US.

deals.asset: IBI363 (PD-1/IL-2 bispecific) and up to 2 other cancer drugs
deals.highlights: Takeda paid $1.2B upfront plus a $100M equity investment for rights to up to three next-generation cancer drugs from Innovent, with milestones up to $10.2B. Lead asset IBI363 (PD-1/IL-2 bispecific) shows potential across multiple solid tumors including in immunotherapy-resistant patients. Takeda called the deal 'transformative' for its oncology portfolio, continuing its China expansion after its 2023 Hutchmed/Fruzaqla acquisition.

Roche secured global rights to Qyuns' dual-targeting TSLP/IL-33 bispecific for COPD and asthma after its own astegolimab failed Phase 3. The deal reflects Roche's continued China sourcing strategy beyond oncology, moving into respiratory diseases. QX031N's novel dual-target mechanism could address inflammation more comprehensively than single-target approaches.

deals.asset: Orelabrutinib (BTK inhibitor) and 2 additional immune drugs
deals.highlights: Zenas BioPharma licensed orelabrutinib (BTK inhibitor) from InnoCare for non-oncology autoimmune indications, with the drug already in Phase 3 for primary progressive MS. The deal includes two additional earlier-stage autoimmune drug candidates, plus equity consideration. Zenas continues to build its pipeline from Chinese sources, having also previously licensed obexelimab from Xencor—a strategy that bets on China's autoimmune innovation.

deals.asset: ADC candidate for colorectal cancer and solid tumors
deals.highlights: Roche paid $80M upfront to Hansoh for ex-Greater China rights to an ADC candidate for colorectal cancer and other solid tumors, with up to $1.45B in milestones and royalties. The drug is in Phase 1 testing in China and the US. Roche has deep CRC experience via Avastin and is adding next-gen ADC technology from China's prolific licensing dealmaker Hansoh, which has inked multiple high-profile deals in oncology and obesity.

deals.asset: IBI363 (PD-1/IL-2 bispecific) and IBI343 (Claudin 18.2 ADC) + option for 3rd candidate
deals.highlights: Takeda paid $1.2B upfront plus a $100M equity investment for ex-Greater China rights to two Innovent cancer candidates (IBI363 and IBI343) plus an option on a third asset, with up to $10.2B in milestones. This transformative deal positions Takeda's post-Entyvio oncology strategy around Chinese-originated biologics. At $11.4B total potential value, it is one of the largest China biotech licensing deals ever, reflecting the sector's maturation from discount generics to premium innovation.

Crescent Biopharma, which went public via reverse merger in June 2025 raising $200M, licensed Kelun-Biotech's ADC to pair with its PD-1xVEGF bispecific. Kelun-Biotech has become a prolific ADC out-licensor. The combination strategy mirrors the emerging oncology approach of pairing ADCs with immune checkpoint bispecifics.

Pfizer turned to China for a second attempt at an oral obesity pill after its internal GLP-1 programs struggled. The deal with a Fosun Pharma subsidiary (Yaopharma) for up to $2B gives Pfizer a new oral weight loss candidate and reflects Big Pharma's willingness to source even in the highly competitive metabolic space from China.

After discontinuing two internal oral GLP-1 candidates due to liver safety issues, Pfizer licensed YaoPharma/Fosun's experimental weight management drug for $150M upfront and up to $1.94B in milestones. This deal underscores Pfizer's desperation to re-enter the oral obesity race and China's growing role as a source of obesity drug candidates.

AstraZeneca paid $100M upfront plus up to $1.91B in milestones for rights to a clinical-stage multitarget asset from Jacobio Pharma. This deal adds to AZ's aggressive China deal-making streak alongside the CSPC obesity portfolio and other partnerships, demonstrating the company's deep commitment to sourcing innovation from Chinese biotechs.

deals.asset: SIM0613 (ADC targeting protein on tumors and cancer-associated fibroblasts)
deals.highlights: Ipsen deepened its push into the ADC space by licensing SIM0613 from Nanjing-based Simcere Zaiming in a deal worth up to $1.06B. The ADC targets a protein highly expressed on multiple tumor types and cancer-associated fibroblasts, potentially offering broad applicability. This was part of a wave of late-2025 China licensing deals by Western pharma companies.

Pfizer paid $150M upfront plus up to $1.94B in milestones and royalties for worldwide rights to YaoPharma's oral GLP-1 agonist YP05002 and related GLP-1 programs. The deal fills a critical gap for Pfizer after it discontinued two internal oral GLP-1 candidates (lotiglipron and danuglipron) due to liver safety concerns. Reflects growing trend of Western pharma turning to Chinese innovators for obesity drugs.

AbbVie paid $100M upfront to Zejing Biopharmaceutical for the option to license alveltamig (ZG006), a DLL3-targeting trispecific T-cell binder being evaluated in late-stage trials for small cell lung cancer and other DLL3-expressing malignancies. The deal highlights the intense competition in DLL3-targeting therapies for SCLC, where multiple companies are racing to develop treatments. AbbVie continues to expand its oncology pipeline through China-originated assets.

ASK Pharm licensed the China rights to Adlai Nortye's preclinical pan-RAS inhibitor AN9025 in a deal worth 1.6 billion CNY (~$230M). AN9025 is designed to target a broad spectrum of RAS mutations across various tumor types. Preclinical studies demonstrate potent and durable efficacy against RAS-mutant cancers. A Phase 1 trial was planned for Q1 2026. This is a notable intra-China/cross-border deal (Adlai Nortye is Hangzhou/New Jersey-based).

Formation Bio's subsidiary Bleecker Bio secured ex-China rights to a next-generation immunology asset from China's Lynk Pharmaceuticals in a deal worth over $600M in biobucks. Lynk gained a minority equity stake in Bleecker Bio. This deal kicked off Formation Bio's China licensing spree, demonstrating the growing trend of AI-driven drug developers sourcing clinical assets from Chinese biotechs.

Pfizer paid $150M upfront to Fosun's YaoPharma subsidiary for worldwide rights to oral GLP-1 agonist YP05002 and related GLP-1 assets. The drug is in Phase 1 for weight management in Australia. This deal reflects Pfizer's aggressive pivot into obesity after internal GLP-1 failures and its $10B acquisition of Metsera. Pfizer is now sourcing obesity assets from China, signaling the breadth of China's innovation in the metabolic/obesity space.

Novartis paid $50M cash upfront for exclusive worldwide rights to PepLib's peptide-based radioligand therapy, with additional biobucks. Announced at JPM26, this deal reflects Novartis's continued push into the RLT space following its Lutathera/Pluvicto franchise. Notable as a Chinese peptide platform licensing to a big pharma leader in radiopharmaceuticals.

deals.chinese_party: Jiangsu Chia Tai Feng Hai Pharmaceutical
deals.highlights: AI-fueled Formation Bio continues its 'China shopping spree' via subsidiary Kenmare Bio, licensing an oral miR-124 activator for autoimmune disease from Jiangsu Chia Tai Feng Hai. With few miR-124 activators in development globally, this represents a differentiated mechanism. Formation Bio's model of licensing China assets and spinning out dedicated subsidiaries is an emerging BD trend.

deals.asset: SYH2082 and obesity/weight management portfolio (8 programs)
deals.upfront_usd: Not disclosed (up to $1.2B in near-term payments)
deals.highlights: The largest-ever China out-licensing deal by total potential value. AstraZeneca licensed CSPC's entire weight management portfolio including clinical-ready SYH2082 and 7 additional programs, with $3.5B in R&D milestones and $13.8B in sales milestones plus royalties. This deal signals AstraZeneca's aggressive push into obesity and complements its existing pipeline (elecoglipron, AZD6234) while validating CSPC's platform approach.

deals.asset: Up to 8 next-generation obesity/weight loss drug programs
deals.highlights: The largest China out-licensing deal by total value since 2025, AstraZeneca paid $1.2B upfront for access to CSPC's platform and up to eight experimental weight loss medications, with up to $3.5B in R&D milestones and $13.8B in sales milestones plus royalties. The deal hands AstraZeneca a broad obesity portfolio at lower cost than an acquisition (Pfizer paid $10B for Metsera). It builds on existing AZ-CSPC AI collaboration and AZ's $15B China investment pledge.

SciNeuro Pharmaceuticals signed a landmark $1.7B deal with Novartis to develop antibody treatments for Alzheimer's disease, receiving $165M upfront plus up to $1.5B in milestones and royalties. SciNeuro will collaborate on early-stage development before Novartis takes over clinical testing and global commercialization. This is one of the largest CNS licensing deals involving a Chinese biotech and reflects growing pharma interest in novel Alzheimer's approaches.

Eli Lilly's seventh collaboration with Innovent Biologics, reflecting deep strategic confidence in the Chinese biotech's pipeline. At $350M upfront with up to $8.5B in milestones, this is one of the largest China out-licensing deals. Innovent leads discovery through clinical proof-of-concept, with Lilly taking over development and commercialization outside China.

AbbVie paid $650M upfront to RemeGen for ex-China rights to RC148, a PD-1xVEGF bispecific, with up to $4.95B in milestones plus double-digit royalties. This deal marks AbbVie's entry into the highly competitive PD-1xVEGF bispecific space, following Akeso/Summit's ivonescimab lead and multiple Chinese-originated competitors. The $650M upfront is among the largest for a PD-1xVEGF asset.

Madrigal Pharmaceuticals struck a licensing deal with CSPC that could be worth over $2B if it results in a new drug for a serious form of liver disease. This is notable as Madrigal is known for its MASH drug Rezdiffra and this deal suggests CSPC's pipeline has assets of interest beyond oncology and metabolic diseases.

Sanofi returned to Earendil Labs (affiliated with China's Helixon Therapeutics) for a second, broader deal applying Earendil's AI-powered discovery platform to generate multiple bispecific autoimmune and inflammatory disease programs. At $2.56B total potential value with $160M near-term, it signals deepening trust in China-linked AI drug discovery. Sanofi will handle all development and worldwide commercialization.

Eisai licensed Henlius' anti-PD-1 antibody Hansizhuang (serplulimab) for the Japanese market, paying $75M upfront plus up to $313.3M in milestones. This deal marks a significant licensing of a Chinese PD-1 antibody into a major regulated market and validates Henlius' oncology portfolio for ex-China commercialization.

Harbour BioMed co-founded Solstice Oncology to advance HBM4003, a next-gen anti-CTLA-4 HCAb (heavy chain-only antibody), outside Greater China. The unique structure allows Harbour to retain equity in the new company while receiving up to $1.1B in milestones plus royalties. HBM4003 is designed to offer improved safety and efficacy over existing CTLA-4 antibodies like ipilimumab, leveraging Harbour's proprietary HCAb platform.

AstraZeneca announced a planned $15B investment to strengthen its China ties, including drug manufacturing and R&D, amid a prolonged surge in dealmaking activity between large pharmaceutical companies and Chinese counterparts. This investment signals AZ's deepening commitment to China as both a market and an innovation hub.

Formation Bio licensed ex-China rights to a next-gen immunology asset from China's Lynk Pharmaceuticals via newly created subsidiary Bleecker Bio, in a deal worth over $600M in biobucks. Lynk received a minority equity stake in Bleecker Bio. This follows Formation's pattern of licensing China-originated assets into dedicated subsidiaries and using AI to accelerate development.

AirNexis launched with $200M and a clinical-stage PDE3/4 inhibitor licensed from China's Haisco Pharmaceutical Group for COPD. The drug is designed to expand airways and reduce inflammation. Haisco received $40M cash and a 20% equity stake in AirNexis, reflecting the growing trend of Chinese biotechs taking equity in US startups built around their assets.

Caldera Therapeutics debuted with $112.5M Series A and a bispecific antibody targeting both IL-23p19 and TL1A licensed from China's Qyuns Therapeutics. CLD-423 addresses two of the hottest targets in IBD simultaneously, differentiating from single-target approaches. Already in Phase 1 in healthy volunteers, this deal taps into the massive TL1A wave following Roche's $7B Telavant acquisition and strong Sanofi/Teva duvakitug data.

Gilead secured global rights to Genhouse Bio's MAT2A-targeting synthetic lethal therapy GH31, paying $80M upfront with up to $1.45B in milestones plus tiered double-digit royalties. The Suzhou-based company had already secured IND clearance in both China and the US. The deal expands Gilead's oncology synthetic lethality strategy as CEO Daniel O'Day said the company approaches dealmaking from 'a position of strength' in 2026.

deals.asset: Six preclinical siRNA programs for MASH
deals.highlights: Madrigal licensed six preclinical siRNA programs from China's Ribo Life Science (via subsidiary Ribocure Pharmaceuticals) to develop next-gen MASH therapies that silence genes driving liver disease progression. The $60M upfront/$4.4B total deal is heavily back-loaded and designed to complement Madrigal's blockbuster Rezdiffra (first FDA-approved MASH drug). Reflects growing Western interest in China's siRNA capabilities beyond ADCs.

deals.asset: Broad oncology and immunology drug discovery alliance
deals.highlights: Eli Lilly's seventh collaboration with Innovent covers a broad alliance for cancer and immunological diseases. Innovent leads discovery through clinical proof-of-concept, then Lilly takes over development and commercialization outside China. The $350M upfront and up to $8.5B in milestones reflect Lilly's deepening strategic relationship with Innovent, alongside the Takeda and Roche deals also signed in 2025.

deals.asset: Multiple bispecific autoimmune/inflammatory programs (AI-discovery platform expansion)
deals.highlights: Sanofi's second deal with Earendil/Helixon applies the AI-driven discovery platform to generate multiple new bispecific antibody candidates for autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. At $160M upfront and up to $2.56B total, this deal is larger than the first April 2025 pact and validates Helixon's AI drug design capabilities. Sanofi has now committed nearly $4.4B in total biobucks to the Earendil/Helixon partnership.

Pfizer will pay up to $495M for partial ownership and exclusive China commercialization rights to ecnoglutide from Hangzhou-based Sciwind Biosciences. The drug is already approved in China for Type 2 diabetes with a weight management application accepted by China's regulator. This is an unusual deal where a Western pharma is licensing IN a China-developed asset for the China market, showing Pfizer's commitment to building its obesity franchise domestically.

deals.asset: Two siRNA therapies targeting kidney diseases
deals.highlights: GSK paid Frontier Biotechnologies $40M upfront for worldwide rights to two siRNA therapies targeting kidney diseases, with up to $963M in milestones plus tiered royalties. One candidate is already in Phase 1 in China, while the other is completing IND-enabling activities. This deal extends GSK's growing siRNA portfolio and reflects the company's aggressive dealmaking under new CEO Luke Miels.

deals.asset: Six preclinical siRNA programs for MASH
deals.highlights: Madrigal licensed six preclinical siRNA programs from China's Ribo Life Science (via Swedish subsidiary Ribocure Pharmaceuticals) in a heavily back-loaded deal worth up to $4.4B. Madrigal aims to develop next-generation siRNA therapies silencing genes implicated in MASH to combine with its blockbuster Rezdiffra. This is Madrigal's second deal with a Chinese biotech, following its $120M CSPC GLP-1 agonist deal in July 2025.

Argo Biopharma expanded its collaboration with Novartis on RNA medicines for cardiovascular diseases, receiving $160M upfront plus Novartis plans to participate in Argo's next financing round. This builds on two previous licensing agreements worth $185M in initial payments from 2025, making Novartis a repeat customer. The deal underscores the growing importance of China-originated RNA therapeutics in cardiometabolic disease.

US startup Slate Medicines launched with $130M Series A and a lead monoclonal antibody licensed from Chinese biotech DartsBio Pharmaceutical. SLTE-1009 targets PACAP, a novel mechanism distinct from CGRP-based migraine drugs like those from Eli Lilly and Amgen. Phase 1 testing expected in mid-2026. This deal illustrates the growing trend of US startups being founded specifically around China-originated assets.
